summary: Priority-1 restore-drill BSON RecursionError fix verified end-to-end. Unit tests (3/3) and live integration tests (4/4) all passed. mongod stayed stable (pid 8958, no SIGABRT) throughout 5 back-to-back drill-now calls plus regression /run and /test-restore. No 502/499 seen.
critical_code_review_comments: restore_drill_cron.py L133-135: fix is correct — shallow-copying attempts breaks self-reference. Consider adding a compact unit assertion inside the module itself (e.g. dev-mode `bson.encode(row)` self-check) if paranoid, but not required.

db_restore.restore_to_scratch consolidation into single tagged collection is a solid FD-exhaustion mitigation for the Preview pod's 1024 ulimit and is Atlas-safe; the __aurem_restore_drill_src__ / __aurem_restore_drill_orig_id__ fields correctly avoid _id collisions across singleton 'global' rows.
_drop_prefixed() sweeping ANY _restore_scratch_-prefixed collection is a good defensive cleanup for prior-run leftovers.

rca_of_the_issue: Original: row['fallback_attempts'] = attempts where row is itself an element of attempts → self-referential dict → pymongo BSON encoder recurses forever → RecursionError on insert_one. Fix: shallow-copy each attempt into a fresh dict before assignment. Verified via bson.encode(row) round-trip in unit test test_fallback_row_is_bson_encodable_no_recursion_error, and via 5 back-to-back live drill-now calls that all returned 200 without crashing mongod.
